decision.question: ChatPanel's API shape
options: A class wrapping chat()+composer() with no local state — caller must always supply source/deliver
A class that keeps its own local entries list by default, usable with zero config, and accepts source/deliver to be driven externally
decision.chose: local list by default (say(entry)), source/deliver optional overrides
decision.why: a later voice-sessions task builds on this component and the brief said keep the API small and documented; a panel usable with zero args is the smallest surface, and every current caller (drawer AI tab, mobile sheet) can still hand it a real source/deliver

decision.question: How the panel's height starts small and grows to a max, then scrolls
options: JS measures scrollHeight and sets an explicit height on scroll/resize
Pure CSS: flex-direction column, max-height on the panel, min-height:0 + flex:1 1 auto on the log so it is the one child that shrinks and scrolls
decision.why: the brief asked for pure CSS where possible, no JS measuring; the flex column + min-height:0 pattern is the standard way to let one child absorb overflow and needs no resize listener

decision.question: How to prove streaming still works once ai.js's non-card reply is a ChatPanel bubble, not a raw DOM node it can .empty() and refill
options: Drop live streaming, only show the final reply
Model each turn as the universal chat line and use its new fix:true replace-in-place rule to redraw the same bubble as chunks arrive
decision.chose: the universal chat line's fix:true rule
decision.why: the parent's own new ask was for ChatPanel to draw this shape for real, and it is exactly the mechanism v1's $reply.empty() was doing by hand — one design, two jobs

decision.question: Universal chat line dedup key, so a fix line is drawn instead of silently dropped as a duplicate
options: Reuse the old key() (type+id+at+ref+text) — collides, every chat-shaped entry looks alike
key on chat.at plus whether the line is a fix
decision.why: two ordinary lines never legitimately share an at; a fix always differs from its original by exactly that flag
